_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401875556.overall: Willem II are bottom of the Eredivisie, have lost six league games in a row and named Jurgen Streppel coach on 28 October, after Adrie Koster's interim spell ended in a 1-6 home defeat to Cambuur. This is Streppel's second game in charge. PEC Zwolle are under caretaker Dennis van der Ree after Henry van der Vegt left and are unbeaten in four league games, but they went out of the cup at TOP Oss last week.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, largely because Willem II have conceded 25 in their last six. A new coach in a relegation scrap usually fixes the defence first, and Zwolle have scored only 6 in their last six, so we lean a little lower. Both defences are weak, though, so this lean is mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners. Nothing in the news changes how either side attacks. Willem II should push at home under Streppel, and Zwolle's 4-3-3 is expected to be unchanged from last weekend.

cards.text: The numbers say about 3 cards. Desperation at the bottom could raise the temperature, but we found nothing on referee Allard Lindhout's style or on any feud between the clubs to move this number.

shots.text: The numbers say 30 shots. Willem II are expected to name an unchanged 4-4-1-1, and Zwolle field their usual side. We found nothing that changes the expected volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. The absences are fringe players: Hoogma and Lachkar for Willem II, and Floranus, Krastev and Rahajaän for Zwolle. None of them changes the attacking quality much.

401884739.overall: This is a relegation six-pointer before the international break. Hamburg are 15th after two straight league defeats and have only four open-play goals this season. Gladbach are bottom but unbeaten in three, with their first clean sheet in a 0-0 at Paderborn. Gladbach coach Alexander Blessin was reported unwell this week, and his side are missing several attackers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Hamburg's attack has been toothless (only Schalke have fewer open-play goals), and Fabio Vieira is still out. Gladbach are without Nicolas Kühn, Hugo Bolin and Tim Kleindienst. With so much at stake at the bottom, a cagey game looks likelier than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Polzin expects an evenly matched game against a pressing Gladbach side, and nothing in the team news points clearly to more or fewer corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. This is a scrap between 15th and 18th: Blessin wants a 'hungry' team, and Polzin's side could drop into the bottom three with a loss. Gladbach's aggressive pressing also tends to produce fouls, so we lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots. Gladbach have lost their main forward options in Kühn, Bolin and Kleindienst (Kleindienst only returns after the break), and Hamburg have struggled to create in open play. Poulsen, Capaldo and Bornauw were all doubtful.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. With Hamburg's weak finishing and Gladbach missing their best attackers, we expect fewer efforts to test either goalkeeper. Gladbach are also without their first-choice keeper, Moritz Nicolas, which may tempt Hamburg to shoot from range.

401876405.overall: Toulouse (12th, 10 points) and Strasbourg (13th, 10 points) meet in midtable. Toulouse lost 2-0 at Marseille after a five-game unbeaten run. Strasbourg ended four straight defeats by beating Auxerre 5-1. Strasbourg's league games have averaged four goals this season (17 scored, 19 conceded in 9).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Strasbourg's games are high-scoring, and their attack looks restored with Doukouré, Nanasi and Godo back for the Auxerre rout. Toulouse lose winger Aron Dønnum to suspension and on-loan Alexis Amougou (ineligible against his parent club), which slightly blunts them, but the Strasbourg factor points up.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners. Both coaches are expected to use their usual systems, and nothing in the news points either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. This is not a grudge or relegation game, and we found nothing on referee Mathieu Vernice's recent form that would move the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots. Strasbourg have only Baldé and Panichelli missing, and Toulouse's probable XI with Tengstedt and Russell-Rowe up front is close to full strength apart from Dønnum.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Strasbourg's attack is in form after scoring five, and their games tend to be open, so we lean slightly higher.

401874815.overall: The bottom two meet: Venezia are last with 3 points and Udinese 19th with 5. Udinese sacked Kosta Runjaic after a 5-2 home defeat to Roma, and Paolo Zanetti makes his debut at the Penzo. Davide Nicola replaced Giovanni Stroppa at Venezia in October. Zanetti says he will keep the back three for now and wants a team that 'runs, works and presses'.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Venezia have scored only 2 in their last six, and Udinese only 3. A new coach's first game in a relegation six-pointer usually starts with caution and a focus on defence. Udinese's leaky defence (23 conceded in 10) is the main risk to this lean.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Both teams play wing-backs (Venezia 3-5-2, Udinese 3-4-2-1), and nothing in the team news changes the expected flow.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards. This is a high-pressure last-v-second-last game, with a new Udinese coach demanding intensity and a small, loud stadium. We expect more fouls and bookings than a normal game. Referee Juan Luca Sacchi's card tendencies were not reported.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.2 shots. Venezia's probable XI with Adams and Yeboah up front is close to full strength. Udinese may be without a fully fit Keinan Davis but have Solet back. Nothing clearly moves the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Both attacks have been among the league's weakest in recent weeks, and Davis's fitness is uncertain. In a cautious six-pointer, we lean slightly lower.

401882809.overall: Sixth-placed Sevilla host a struggling Alavés side under Quique Sánchez Flores. Coach Luis García Plaza spent three years at Alavés. Both camps are affected by the death of former Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel, and García Plaza said the game should not have been played. Sevilla are without Peque (hamstring), which the site's list misses, plus Marcão, Miguel Sierra and the suspended Manu Bueno.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Alavés have scored just 4 in their last six, and Quique's priority is rebuilding defensive solidity and confidence. Sevilla lose Peque's creativity, and Isaac Romero is carrying a knee knock. García Plaza himself admits Sevilla aren't scoring enough when they dominate.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners. García Plaza describes Alavés as a five-at-the-back side with big target forwards and a heavy reliance on crosses, which tends to produce corners. Sevilla also expect to have long spells of possession at home.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already high. García Plaza expects players on both sides to be cautious after this week's tragedy, but Sevilla games have been heated (Bueno's red at Getafe). These roughly cancel out.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.3 shots. Sevilla may pair Robbie Ure with Stassin or Romero, and Alavés have everyone available except long-term absentees Mikel Rodríguez and Facundo Garcés. Nothing clearly moves the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. Losing Peque and doubts over Romero slightly weaken Sevilla's finishing. A home side that has dominated games recently offsets that, so we stay with the number.

401879242.overall: Everton (7th, 13 points) come in after a 1-0 win at Newcastle that ended a two-game league losing run; David Moyes's side have kept four clean sheets and their league games have averaged about two goals. Coventry (16th) have won three of their last five under Frank Lampard, the former Everton boss, but have failed to score in five of nine league games and have scored only twice in four away matches. Coventry are without Amenda, Woolfenden, Eccles and Haji Wright, Bobby Thomas and Onyeka are doubts, and Jack Grealish's return for Everton after a disciplinary absence is unclear.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Everton keep winning by narrow margins (1-0 at Newcastle, 1-0 against Ipswich and Wolves), their league games average about two goals, and they have four clean sheets in nine. Coventry have drawn a blank in five of nine and scored just twice away from home, so a tight, low-scoring night looks more likely than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Everton should have more of the ball against a Coventry side expected to sit in with Awoniyi as their lone outlet, but the news gives no clear reason to move far from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already raised for Stuart Attwell's record. Lampard's return to his old club adds some edge, but neither side is described as card-prone, and the news gives no reason to move the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots. Everton should take most of them against a Coventry back line missing Amenda and Woolfenden and possibly Bobby Thomas, but Moyes's side often settle for control once ahead, which keeps the total around the model's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. Thierno Barry leads Everton's attack and Awoniyi leads Coventry's, but the news gives no clear reason to move this number either way.

401885399.overall: The table has turned the model's history around: Arouca are 5th with 20 points and have won four in a row since Vítor Severino took over without conceding a league goal, while Famalicão are 11th on 10 points. Famalicão lost 3-0 at Braga last time out, are led by interim coach Ricardo Silva (whose future will be decided after this game), had no rest day before this Friday match and are without the suspended Rodrigo Pinheiro. Arouca are missing Puche and Pedro Santos through injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Arouca have not conceded a league goal in four games under Severino, who says this match needs a careful plan of knowing when to attack space and when to drop off. Famalicão have just been beaten 3-0 by Braga, are without Pinheiro and are playing on short rest, which points to a cagey game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. If Arouca sit deeper as Severino suggested, Famalicão may win more corners at home, but their attacking form has dipped, so the two effects roughly cancel.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already high for this fixture's history and Arouca's recent bookings. With an interim coach playing for his job there is pressure, but nothing in the news clearly pushes the number higher or lower.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.7 shots. Arouca's recent run has been built on defensive control, and a tired Famalicão side playing on short rest after the Braga defeat may struggle to create much volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. Arouca's four straight clean sheets under Severino suggest they limit good chances, and Famalicão are missing Pinheiro, so a slightly lower figure looks reasonable.

401878758.overall: Leeds have gone five league games without a win and Daniel Farke admits his attack is 'still struggling a little bit'. Tottenham under Roberto De Zerbi arrive on three straight wins, and this is their last game before the international break. Leeds expect Joe Rodon back, but Farke has 'major doubts' over Anton Stach (foot), Noah Okafor (adductor) has only done individual work, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin had a small foot setback. Spurs get Rodrigo Bentancur back from a three-match ban and Tosin Adarabioyo back in training, but are still without Bergvall, Sávio, Xavi Simons, Odobert and Mudryk.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Leeds have scored twice in five games, and with Stach and probably Okafor missing and Calvert-Lewin not fully fit, they have little attacking threat. Spurs have conceded once in three games. Maddison is expected to start for Spurs, but they are still missing Simons, Odobert and Mudryk, so we expect a fairly tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Spurs should see more of the ball, and Leeds will rely on wing-backs Bogle and Gudmundsson for width. That matches what the model already expects.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, already raised for John Brooks's record. Bentancur's return from his red-card ban adds some bite to the Spurs midfield, but nothing else in the news moves the number either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. Farke says his attack is still struggling, and with Okafor and Stach doubtful, Leeds may not test Spurs often. Spurs are also short of wide attackers, so the total looks slightly high.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. A blunt Leeds attack facing a Spurs defence that has conceded once in three games points to fewer clear efforts than the model expects.

401882812.overall: Málaga are bottom with 5 points after five draws and six defeats, and have not won at La Rosaleda this season. Juanfran Funes calls it 'a test of persistence and resilience' and is hoping for a first win. Racing (16th, 11 points) lost 0-3 to Real Madrid and have lost all five away games. They are without Álvaro Mantilla and Andrés Martín, while Málaga have fitness doubts over Carlos Puga, Joaquín Muñoz and Pablo Martínez on top of the long-term absences.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Racing's away record (five defeats out of five) and Málaga's need to win both point to goals. Against that, Málaga have scored only six in their last six, and Racing are without Andrés Martín, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 13.2 corners, already very high. Málaga should push hard at home, with David Larrubia running at defenders, but that is already in the model, and the doubts over Puga and Joaquín Muñoz could take some width out of their play.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, raised now that Isidro Díaz de Mera has been named referee. A tense game for a winless team at the bottom fits that number, but the news gives no reason to go above it.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.9 shots. Funes expects a 'partidazo' against a Racing side that likes to play, and Racing have been open away from home. Without Andrés Martín, Racing will produce less, which balances things out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Both defences have let through plenty of chances, which the model already reflects, and the team news does not clearly change the picture.

401874791.overall: Frosinone (Massimiliano Alvini) are sixth with 20 points after back-to-back wins and come in as the in-form side. Cagliari have been stuck on 13 points under Fabio Pisacane. They are missing Mina, Nzola, Fadera and suspended Obert, which leaves Mendy as the lone striker in a 4-3-2-1. Frosinone are without striker Antonio Raimondo, and Birligea is slightly favoured over Bobcek to replace him.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already lowered for Raimondo and Nzola being out. Frosinone's attack is flying and Cagliari have leaked goals, but Cagliari have few forwards to pick from, so the model's middle ground looks right.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners. Frosinone's 4-2-3-1 with Ghedjemis and Kvernadze out wide should earn corners, which the model already accounts for.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already raised a lot for referee Giovanni Ayroldi. Cagliari's winless run adds some pressure, but nothing in the news points clearly either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.8 shots, pushed up mainly by Frosinone's last six games. Cagliari play with a single striker (Mendy) and Frosinone are without Raimondo, so that total looks stretched.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Both sides are missing a first-choice striker (Nzola for Cagliari, Raimondo for Frosinone), which points to a slightly lower figure.

401874811.overall: Torino (Ignazio Abate) have lost two in a row after three straight wins, and will be without Rolando Mandragora, who is aiming to return after the international break. Lecce (Eusebio Di Francesco) are fighting relegation after three straight defeats, including 5-1 at Frosinone. Pierotti, Berisha, Geubbels and Monteiro are listed as unavailable. Torino are expected to play a 3-4-1-2 with Vlasic behind Adams and Simeone.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Lecce's defence has been leaking, but their attack is weakened without Pierotti, Berisha and Geubbels. Torino are without Mandragora in midfield, so the two effects roughly cancel out.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Torino's wing-backs and Lecce's 4-3-3 are their usual shapes, and none of the team news points clearly to more or fewer corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.1 cards, which looks low for a Serie A game with this much at stake. Lecce are in a relegation scrap after three straight defeats and Torino need a reaction after two losses, so we expect a scrappy game. Ermanno Feliciani referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots. Torino should have the edge at home with Adams, Simeone and Vlasic, while Lecce's weakened attack balances that out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. The team news doesn't give a clear reason to move away from the model.

401884737.overall: Promoted Paderborn have drawn 0-0 in their last two league games and have won both home games this season. Adi Hütter calls them 'extremely unpleasant' at home, with a high press and a 5-3-2, and says Frankfurt must bring intensity and win lots of duels in a match he calls 'richtungsweisend' (one that sets the direction). Mario Götze is out with an ear infection and captain Robin Koch (knee knock) is in a race to be fit. Hütter has not said whether Ebnoutalib and Burkardt will start together.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Paderborn come in on two goalless draws and Hütter expects a grind, with high pressing and lots of duels. Frankfurt are also without Götze as a creator, so we expect a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Paderborn's 5-3-2 relies on wing-backs for width, which the model already reflects, and nothing in the team news moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards, which looks low for a game like this. Paderborn press high and Hütter says Frankfurt must win the battle of duels, which tends to bring fouls and bookings. Bastian Dankert referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 30 shots. Paderborn's recent games have been low-event (two 0-0 draws), and Frankfurt are without Götze, so a stop-start, physical game should produce fewer shots than the model expects.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Two goalless draws in a row for Paderborn and Götze's absence for Frankfurt point to slightly fewer clear efforts.

401884740.overall: Bayern are still without Vincent Kompany, who is recovering from a viral inflammation of the brain membranes, so Aaron Danks leads the team again. Danks said Díaz, Gnabry, Musiala and Saibari remain out, Pavlovic is fit to start, and Alphonso Davies may be rested after a long run of midweek games. Mainz lost three games in a week. Urs Fischer wants his side to get back to basics, with 'running, duels, intensity, aggression', and he has to rebuild his back line without the suspended Posch and Mwene.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals. Mainz have conceded 17 in their last six, and with Posch and Mwene suspended Fischer has to bring in Stefan Bell or Rael Nakuzola at the back, which points up. Bayern are missing four attackers and Danks is managing workloads before the international break, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Bayern should have most of the ball against a Mainz side focused on defending, and nothing in the news moves the corner figure either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Fischer has asked for aggression and hard duels, and local reports say Mainz plan to be 'eklig' (nasty to play against), with a reshuffled defence chasing Bayern's attackers. That points to more fouls and bookings than usual. Robert Schröder referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots. Bayern have scored 18 in their last six and face a weakened Mainz back line. Possible rotation (Davies may be rested) and the missing attackers stop us going higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.7 shots on target. A makeshift Mainz defence should concede chances, but Bayern's thin front line and their tired legs after Tuesday's win at Atlético balance that out.

401884744.overall: Leipzig lost 3-2 to Manchester City on Wednesday, their fourth straight midweek game. Martín Demichelis said the squad trained for only 25 minutes afterwards and he wants 'a fresh team on the pitch', so rotation is likely. Antonio Nusa, who has started every league game, came off against City with muscle problems: Demichelis said Nusa was 'at his limit' and will be assessed on matchday. Manuel Baum's Augsburg are winless in six league games but their matches are open: 3-2, 2-2, 4-3, 1-1 and 1-2 in the last five. Augsburg are without the suspended Juma Bah plus Banks and Brackelmann.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals. Augsburg's recent games have been high-scoring, and their defence is missing Bah, Banks and Brackelmann. A tired, rotated Leipzig possibly without Nusa pulls the other way, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Leipzig should still control territory at home, and the news gives no clear reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. Augsburg's reshuffled back line could lead to some tactical fouls, but there is no specific news on discipline. Daniel Schlager referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots. Demichelis described the workload as extremely high and plans to change his line-up, and Nusa, his most dangerous winger, may sit out. A tired, rotated Leipzig is likely to produce fewer attempts than usual.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.9 shots on target. Augsburg's weakened defence and Leipzig's fatigue roughly cancel out.

401884745.overall: Dortmund are unbeaten in the league (five wins, three draws) but are without Serhou Guirassy (muscle strain), Emre Can, Lerma and Konstantelias. Fabio Silva, who has six goals and three assists this season, is expected to lead the line, and Kovac could rotate after Tuesday's Champions League win over Betis. Promoted Elversberg are seventh, have scored and conceded 16 goals each in eight games, and are expected to use a 4-2-3-1 with Keidel and Poreba shielding the defence.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already lower than yesterday's figure. Without Guirassy, Dortmund have scored only seven league goals in their last six. But Elversberg have scored three or more in four of their eight league games and concede plenty, and Fabio Silva is in form, so we now stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.1 corners. Elversberg's double pivot is set up to deny Dortmund space through the middle, which should push the home side wide and into crosses. That fits the model's high Dortmund corner count.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. There is no specific news on discipline. Harm Osmers referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots. Dortmund should still pile up attempts at home, though without Guirassy the quality is likely to drop more than the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Dortmund lose their main finisher in Guirassy, and possible rotation and tiredness after the Champions League could cost them sharpness. Elversberg's compact midfield should force more efforts from distance.

401878760.overall: League leaders Arsenal (24 points, eight wins in nine) host promoted Hull, who are 11th and winless in six league games (four draws). Arteta confirmed Ezri Konsa is fine after being taken off as a precaution in Prague, Ben White is back, and Saliba is in contention, so only Saka (thigh/quad, out until after the break) and the suspended Dowman are missing. Hull have seven players injured, including goalkeeper Jack Butland, who one report says could still play, and Matt Crooks is suspended.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Arsenal control games rather than run up scores, and Saka's absence removes their main creator. Hull have scored only 11 in nine league games and draw a lot. Sergej Jakirovic admits he found no weakness in Arsenal and wants to make the game uncomfortable for them, which points to a low-scoring match.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10 corners, most of them Arsenal's. Arteta wants his side to attack from the start, and Hull, with seven players injured, are likely to sit deep. That points to Arsenal pinning them back and forcing plenty of blocked crosses and set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, mostly from Hull. Hull lose their combative midfielder Matt Crooks to suspension, and a one-sided game in which Arsenal keep the ball usually produces few flashpoints. Farai Hallam referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. A deep Hull block suits a high Arsenal shot count, and Arsenal's defence is close to full strength. Missing Saka pulls the other way, so the model's figure looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Without Saka, Arsenal lose their main source of chances from the right, and a packed Hull defence should block plenty. Hull rarely test goalkeepers away from home.

401879241.overall: Fulham (15th, 9 points) host Newcastle (13th, 11 points), who lost twice to Everton in a week, in the league and the Carabao Cup. Reports already link Matthias Jaissle's job to other names. Newcastle are without Joelinton, Livramento, Jaouen and the suspended Jacob Ramsey. Lewis Miley and Matias Fernandez-Pardo are back in training but not certain to play. Alvaro Arbeloa says Fulham must keep believing in how they play but need to improve their finishing. Fulham have scored one goal or fewer in each of their last six games, and one report says Ryan Sessegnon is suspended after a red card.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Fulham have scored only five in their last six, and Arbeloa himself names finishing as the problem. Newcastle have six in six and are missing midfielders. Two nervous sides near the bottom half point to a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say about 11 corners, split fairly evenly. Nothing in the team news clearly moves this figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Robert Jones referees a tense game, and Newcastle had Ramsey sent off last time out. Without Ramsey and Joelinton, though, Newcastle lose two of their most combative midfielders, so we stay close to the model.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Newcastle's makeshift midfield, likely Willock and the 18-year-old Sean Steur, should create less. Jaissle says he will accept more long balls to avoid losing possession, which usually means fewer shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Both sides' finishing has been poor: Newcastle are well below their expected goals and Fulham's attack has stalled. That points to fewer efforts on target than the model expects.

401882813.overall: This is Eder Sarabia's first game in charge of Espanyol, who are 14th on 11 points after sacking Manolo González following a cup exit to Sestao River. Sarabia is serving the last game of a touchline ban carried over from Elche, so the site's 'Eder Sarabia suspended' entry is a coaching ban, not a player absence. Sarabia says he will change things gradually and wants a brave, proactive team that keeps the solidity of the previous regime. Antonio Hidalgo's Deportivo are eighth on 14 points. The round goes ahead despite the players' union asking for it to be postponed after the death of Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Espanyol are without striker Kike García (torn hamstring tendon) and winger Jofre Carreras, who is listed out with an adductor problem. They have scored only five in their last six. Deportivo lose centre-back Bright Ede but also forward Zakaria Eddahchouri (hand fracture), and Hidalgo is being careful with Aubameyang. With a new coach whose first priority is not to lose, we expect a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10.7 corners, split almost evenly. Sarabia wants Espanyol on the front foot, but he says he will make changes gradually rather than overhaul the side in his first week. Nothing in the news moves the total clearly.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, about normal for LaLiga, with Alejandro Quintero González refereeing. A new coach and a nervous home crowd near the bottom could add intensity. Against that, Espanyol lose Roger Hinojo to a yellow-card suspension and the weekend's sombre mood may calm things, so we stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Sarabia's proactive approach could raise Espanyol's attempts, but they are missing Kike García and Carreras, and Deportivo are short in attack too. The two effects roughly cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9 shots on target. Both sides are missing a first-choice forward: Kike García for Espanyol and Eddahchouri for Deportivo, while Aubameyang is being managed. Espanyol's finishing has been poor, so we expect slightly fewer efforts on target than the model.

401875555.overall: Danny Buijs's Fortuna Sittard are sixth and unbeaten in six league games after a 1-1 draw at Feyenoord last weekend. A win would lift them above AZ into fifth, but they have taken only seven points from 15 at home. Henk Brugge's Telstar are near the bottom. They beat Utrecht 4-2 but then went out of the KNVB Beker to Almere City in midweek, and they are without Patrick Brouwer, Rui Mendes and Gerald Alders.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. Fortuna have the lowest possession in the league and play a compact, counter-attacking game.
